title: Core Validation 009A Bridge — Right-Side Collapse Robustness
decision_question: Why did Core Validation 009A require a wide left/output-effect space but an apparently near-one-dimensional right/input-condition space, and does that right-side collapse survive controls for activation mean, anisotropy, whitening and sequence averaging?

scope.purpose: Distinguish robust common-right functional geometry from activation-coordinate or sequence-aggregation confounds before designing 009B sparsity/addressability experiments.

data.selection_and_partition: exact Core 006/007/009A pinned sequence selection and train/eval partition

replication.seed_policy: Reuse the exact positive 009A confirmation seeds because this bridge explains an already-observed result; these are not fresh confirmatory seeds.
replication.formal_hardware: Kaggle GPU for frozen gradient/write extraction; all bridge geometry after extraction is CPU-safe

write_geometry.projected_gradient: q_t = U^T dL/dh_t on the frozen foundation path
write_geometry.raw_sequence_write: G_i = mean_t[q_t z_t^T], normalized by Frobenius norm exactly as Core 009A
write_geometry.token_write: g_t = q_t z_t^T; token-normalized spectra use g_t/||g_t||_F and energy-weighted spectra use unnormalized g_t^T g_t
write_geometry.sequence_covariance: C_R = mean_i G_i^T G_i over training sequences
write_geometry.token_energy_weighted_covariance: C_R_token_energy proportional to sum_t g_t^T g_t

controls.whitened: z'_t = (z_t - mean_train(z)) C_train^{-1/2}; eigenvalues are floored before inversion
controls.mean_direction_removed: z'_t = z_t (I - m_hat m_hat^T), where m_hat is the normalized train-token mean direction

top1_ablation.basis_source: top right eigenvector of raw normalized training sequence-write covariance
measure: heldout residual local-action fraction ||Z G_res^T||/||Z G^T||
right spectrum of normalized residual training writes

primary: sequence-write right top-1/top-8 cumulative energy under each z control
token-normalized and token-energy-weighted right top-1/top-8 energy under each z control
heldout right-only residual at n in {1,2,4,8}
alignment: raw sequence right-PC1 vs train-token mean direction
raw sequence right-PC1 vs raw token-normalized right-PC1
raw sequence right-PC1 vs raw token-energy-weighted right-PC1
raw sequence right-PC1 vs top eigenvector of uncentered z second moment
raw sequence right-PC1 vs top eigenvector of centered z covariance
diagnostics.whole_model_nll: not measured; the bridge diagnoses local write geometry only

descriptive_flags.note: These thresholds generate diagnostic labels only. They are frozen before GPU execution but never produce a scientific supported/not-supported decision.

interpretation_boundary: This bridge cannot revoke, weaken or strengthen the formal 009A support decision; it only explains the observed asymmetry.
A large collapse reduction after centering or whitening is evidence that activation coordinates/anisotropy materially contribute to the near-one-dimensional right spectrum.
A much stronger sequence-level collapse than token-level collapse is evidence that sequence averaging or q-z correlation/cancellation contributes materially.

Persistence after centering, whitening and mean-direction removal is evidence for a robust common-right write geometry under these controls, but is still not evidence for sparse routing or continual learning.

A small residual local-action fraction after removing raw right-PC1 means the common right direction dominates local functional action; a large residual means substantial functional structure remains outside the first direction.
Whitening and centering are diagnostic reparameterizations/ablations, not claims that they preserve the exact original operator semantics.
stop_rule: Always report diagnostic evidence with scientific_decision=false. Use the completed bridge only to choose the hypothesis tested by a later 009B; do not retrofit Core 009A gates, dimensions or winner selection.
